nodes.title: Stable compactification of a stable input family
nodes.statement: Let B be Spec Z or Spec k for an arbitrary field k, S an integral quasi-projective B-scheme and C→S a stable genus-g family, g≥2. There exist a normal integral scheme S′, a finite surjective map p:S′→S, an open immersion j:S′→S̄′ with S̄′ normal integral projective over B, and a stable family C̄′→S̄′ whose restriction is isomorphic to C×_S S′. The construction preserves an already nodal family; smooth generic fibre is not required.
hypotheses: Integral means reduced and irreducible; finite type is included in quasi-projective. A compactification is over the same B.
The finite projective cover V→M̄_g is a representable finite surjective map to the stack, carrying the universal stable family.
proofSteps: Choose a projective B-compactification S̄₀. In W=S×_{M̄_g}V choose a reduced irreducible component W₀ dominating S. Its field L=K(W₀) is finite over K(S).
The stack diagonal is finite, so W→S×_B V is finite, not generally a monomorphism. Let D be the integral reduced closure of its W₀-image in S̄₀×_B V. Define S̄′ to be the normalization of D in L.

D is excellent and Nagata. The exact SF.0 finite-normalization target gives a finite S̄′→D, hence projectivity. Over S the result is the normalization of W₀, with a finite surjective map to S. Both normalizations use L; normalization in K(D) can discard isomorphism data.
Pull the stable universal curve on V to S̄′. The defining stack fibre product supplies the isomorphism on S′. None of these steps uses smoothness of the initial family.
acceptance: For C=C₀×A¹ with fixed stable C₀, S̄′ has dimension1. Closing only the point [C₀] does not pass.

Over a field of characteristic≠2, a quadratic twist of a genus2 curve with automorphism group {±1} can become isomorphic to the original curve only over a quadratic field L. The corresponding isomorphism component in the stack fibre product has field L, while its image point has the smaller field. The normalization must retain L.
For a stable C₀ with a node, the constant family over A¹ is accepted; no smooth-generic restriction is introduced.

nodes.title: Full-level Torelli by the relative Jacobian
nodes.statement: Fix g≥2, N≥3 and B_N=Spec Z[1/N,ζ_N] with the chosen primitive root specifying the symplectic pairing. For the MC.4 universal smooth curve f:C_g[N]→M_g[N], use JC1 to form J=Pic⁰_{C/M}, its canonical principal polarization and the induced full symplectic level. Its PEL classifying map τ_N:M_g[N]→A_g[N] has a canonical isomorphism J≅M_g[N]×_{A_g[N]}A_g[N]^univ preserving polarization and level. Formation is natural under every test-scheme pullback; it does not choose a section of C.
hypotheses: Both source and target use the same fixed cyclotomic pairing component. N is invertible on B_N.
The fine Siegel target can first be used as an algebraic space: its good-base scheme realization is a PEL M6/C5 import, not a prerequisite for the classifying map.
proofSteps: Import the family Picard construction and its base change. Use the canonical polarization descended from local theta data; there is no global Abel–Jacobi base point.
Transfer the curve level to its Jacobian torsion with the agreed Weil pairing. Apply fine ppav representability to the object (J,λ,α).
The universal property supplies the Cartesian family comparison and its identity/composition coherence, rather than just agreement on geometric points.
acceptance: A genus≥2 family without a section still has τ_N and the Cartesian Jacobian comparison.
A map from Spec k[ε]/(ε²) is tested by pullback of the same relative Picard object, not just a pointwise Jacobian assignment.
Changing ζ_N changes the paired base/component; a map between mismatched pairing components is rejected.

nodes.title: Canonical Hodge comparison on the fine moduli scheme
nodes.statement: For τ_N above, let E_A=e*Ω¹_{A_g[N]^univ/A_g[N]}, E_C=f_*ω_{C/M}, and λ_A=det E_A, λ_C=det E_C. There are canonical coherent isomorphisms τ_N*E_A≅E_C and τ_N*λ_A≅λ_C. Their pullback along every T→M_g[N], including nonreduced T, is the relative Jacobian Hodge comparison for C_T. Both bundles have rank g; the second comparison is its determinant.
hypotheses: g≥2, N≥3 and B_N as above; M_g[N] is regular, Noetherian and quasi-compact.
The integral-base JC6 theorem is applied on integral open-and-closed components of this fine scheme, not to an arbitrary test scheme T.
proofSteps: Regular local rings are integrally closed domains. SF.0 identifies finitely many disjoint integral open-and-closed components; no geometric irreducibility theorem is required.
Apply JC6 on each component to identify e*Ω¹_J with (R¹f_*O_C)∨≅f_*ω. Use the Cartesian Jacobian comparison to identify the left side with τ_N*E_A.
Glue the canonical componentwise maps. Pull this map and the represented Picard/base-change comparisons to arbitrary T; do not reapply an integral theorem to nonreduced T.
Take the fixed-rank determinant using the existing AlgebraicVectorBundles L0C functor imported by MC.5. Identity and composition coherence come from the same natural maps.
acceptance: On two disconnected integral components the maps glue componentwise, without assuming the full fine scheme integral.
For a dual-number test base the same comparison survives and its reduction agrees with the geometric comparison.
In genus2 the bundle rank is2 but its determinant rank is1; replacing E by λ fails.

nodes.title: The sign ambiguity in geometric Torelli fibres
nodes.statement: Over an algebraically closed field k of arbitrary characteristic with N invertible, the fibre of τ_N over a geometric point is empty or has at most two geometric points. If a preimage is (C,α), the possible points are (C,α) and (C,−α). They are distinct precisely when C is nonhyperelliptic; for hyperelliptic C the hyperelliptic involution identifies them. In genus2 every C is hyperelliptic, so the map is injective on geometric points. Thus τ_N is quasi-finite. No assertion of reduced fibres, separability or proper finiteness is made.
hypotheses: g≥2, N≥3, p∤N, and the fixed symplectic pairing convention of τ_N.
Use strong Torelli including its ± uniqueness statement, not merely injectivity of the curve-isomorphism-class map.
proofSteps: Request strong Torelli from the Jacobian owner. Compare two polarized Jacobian isomorphisms using the induced curve isomorphism up to sign.
Transport full level across that curve isomorphism. The only remaining possibilities are α and −α. For N≥3 these levels differ as torsion trivializations, including in characteristic2.

Strong Torelli says −1 is induced by a curve automorphism exactly in the hyperelliptic case. The resulting point count and finite-type morphism give quasi-finiteness; no infinitesimal-fibre conclusion follows.
acceptance: For a nonhyperelliptic genus3 curve and N=3 there are two different curve-level points with the same ppav-level image.
For a genus2 curve and any allowed N there is one point in a nonempty fibre.
Characteristic2 with odd N is allowed: multiplication by −1 on étale N-torsion is not multiplication by1.
A compact-type degeneration of a smooth genus2 curve to two elliptic components has decomposable Jacobian in A₂ but no smooth preimage there; smooth Torelli is not proper.

nodes.title: Stable Picard and Hodge comparison along a moduli atlas
nodes.statement: Let U→M̄_g be a quasi-compact regular Noetherian smooth scheme atlas over Z, g≥2, and R=U×_{M̄_g}U. On integral open-and-closed components of U and R the R11.4 stable-family Picard and JC6 comparison identify e*Ω¹_{Pic⁰} with f_*ω. Canonical pullback isomorphisms of the represented relative Picard functor identify the two objects on R and satisfy the cocycle on triple overlaps. They descend a semiabelian Picard group object over the stack and its rank-g Hodge comparison. For any test scheme T→M̄_g the comparison is the pullback one for the classified stable curve, including nonreduced T; a scheme-representability claim on T requires the R11.4 arbitrary-base export, not algebraic-space descent alone.
hypotheses: The MC.1 atlas is smooth over the regular base Z and finite type; its overlaps are representable schemes and regular Noetherian.
The required arbitrary-base Picard identification and effective scheme representability are the precise R11.4 request. Preserve its early semiabelian and normalization-cohomology gaps.
proofSteps: Use regularity and the exact SF.0 component criterion on U, R and triple overlaps; apply integral-base R11.4 and JC6 componentwise.
All comparison maps arise from pullback of the same fppf Picard sheaf and the natural Lie/cohomology map. Hence they agree on overlaps and satisfy the cocycle before taking determinants.

Use algebraic-space group descent and quasi-coherent descent for the stack object and Hodge isomorphism. Ask R11.4 for the additional stable-curve arbitrary-base scheme representation; do not infer it from algebraic-space descent.
For arbitrary T, pull back the canonical atlas descent and compare its represented Picard functor. This transfers the formula without assuming T integral or regular.
acceptance: For a stable one-node irreducible genus2 curve with elliptic normalization, the semiabelian fibre has torus rank1 and abelian rank1, but its Hodge rank is2.
For two elliptic components joined at one separating node, torus rank is0 and Pic⁰ is their product.
A stable degeneration with local total-space equation xy=t² has nonregular total space at the node; it still lies in the source range.
On a nonreduced test scheme only the canonical pullback comparison is used; splitting it into integral components is invalid.

nodes.title: The abelian part of a stable Jacobian
nodes.statement: For a stable connected curve C of genus g≥2 over an algebraically closed field k, let ν:⊔_v C̃_v→C be its normalization and Γ its dual multigraph, allowing loops. There is a canonical fppf exact sequence 1→T_Γ→Pic⁰_C→∏_v J(C̃_v)→0, with X*(T_Γ)=H₁(Γ,Z). Put r=b₁(Γ) and a=Σ_v g(C̃_v)=g−r. The abelian quotient has the product principal polarization and defines a point of the a-dimensional ppav stratum of A_g^min. Hodge rank of Pic⁰_C remains g, not a.
hypotheses: Vertices index geometric irreducible components; edges index nodes, including self-nodes.
The normalized component Jacobians and their principal polarizations are imports, not reconstructed here.
proofSteps: Import the R11.4 units/cohomology exact sequence and graph-character calculation, retaining the recorded normalization proof leaf.
Use arithmetic-genus additivity to identify g=a+r. Give the abelian quotient the product polarization; its determinant differential is not the whole rank-g semiabelian Hodge bundle.
Apply the C5 Siegel minimal-stratum interpretation by the abelian part. No claim that the nonproper generalized Jacobian itself lies in A_g is made.
acceptance: An irreducible stable genus2 curve with one node and elliptic normalization maps to the A₁ stratum, and X*(T)=Z.
A union of two elliptic curves meeting at one node maps to their product in the interior A₂ (compact type).
A rational curve with two self-nodes is stable of genus2: X*(T)=Z², abelian quotient0, and the minimal image lies in A₀. Counting only edges between different components fails.

nodes.title: Compactified Torelli in every characteristic
nodes.statement: For every algebraically closed field k and g≥2 construct t̄_g:M̄_g^coarse→A_g^min over k, extending coarse smooth Torelli. Its value on a stable curve C is the principally polarized abelian part ∏_v J(C̃_v) in the A_a stratum, a=g−b₁(Γ). The stack morphism is defined by canonical semiabelian specialization on regular atlases and descends by the coarse universal property. It is independent of the atlas, finite stable-family cover and any toroidal cone choices; it commutes with extension of algebraically closed fields.
hypotheses: A_g^min is the fixed-field unlevelled Siegel coarse minimal space requested from C5, supported by FC V2.3 over Z and a proved fixed-field comparison. A literal identification with a geometric fibre of the integral model is not assumed; a characteristic-zero Satake theorem alone does not supply this target.
The C5 normal-base semiabelian extension and Hodge-power contract is an explicit supplier gap. No use is made of FC V6.7 in characteristic p.
Coarse formation is used over fixed k and permitted flat field extension; no arbitrary nonflat base-change theorem is asserted.
proofSteps: On each integral regular atlas component use its stable Picard semiabelian scheme, generically a canonically polarized abelian scheme. Request the C5 extension of the generic classifying map to the minimal space, together with its Hodge-power comparison.

Uniqueness and the canonical Picard overlap isomorphisms make these maps agree on double overlaps. Descend the stack map; the categorical coarse universal property factors it uniquely through M̄_g^coarse.
At geometric boundary points apply the abelian-part stratum rule. On the smooth open this is the JC1 Jacobian, so the result extends smooth Torelli.
FC IV5.1 requires a common toroidal cone on a general normal base. Independence after contraction to the minimal space must be proved by the supplier; a direct toroidal lift is not silently assumed.
acceptance: A separating elliptic–elliptic genus2 boundary curve maps into A₂, not the lower-dimensional boundary.
A rational stable genus2 curve with two nodes maps into A₀.
Moving the attaching points of two fixed smooth components leaves the product-Jacobian image fixed; compactified Torelli need not have finite fibres.
A characteristic2 example is covered by the all-Z minimal target and the requested semiabelian extension contract, not by characteristic-zero purity.

nodes.title: Stable Hodge as a minimal Hodge pullback
nodes.statement: Over the k of minimal-torelli-descent, let q:M̄_g→M̄_g^coarse and λ=det(f_*ω). There exist m>0 and an ample invertible sheaf A on A_g^min such that (t̄_g∘q)*A≅λ^⊗m canonically with the semiabelian Hodge comparison. Equivalently, λ descends as a rational line λ_coarse with λ_coarse=t̄_g*ω_min and ω_min ample as a rational line. For every stable family over a projective k-scheme X this yields λ_X^⊗m≅h_X*A; the comparison survives nonreduced test pullback. The power absorbs stabilizer actions and toric determinant signs.
hypotheses: A and m are chosen compatibly from the Siegel minimal Hodge-power theorem; the unlevelled coarse Hodge line need not itself descend integrally.
Use the rank-g semiabelian invariant-differential determinant across the boundary, not the smaller-rank abelian-part differential determinant.
proofSteps: Request the all-characteristic Siegel minimal ample power and its pullback identification on semiabelian normal bases. Compare this semiabelian Hodge line with the stable Hodge line by atlas-comparison.

Glue the canonical positive-power isomorphisms on overlaps and factor the target morphism through the coarse space. This directly supplies a descending power of λ, without an unsupported wild coarse-line descent assertion.
For a family pull back the stack equality. Rationalize the line group only after the positive-power statement, with coherent determinant base change.
acceptance: At an irreducible nodal genus2 curve the rank2 semiabelian determinant is used although the abelian quotient has dimension1.
For two components of genera g₁,g₂ the determinant symmetry contains (−1)^(g₁g₂); a suitable positive power absorbs this sign on coarse descent.
For a family over dual numbers the equality is an invertible-sheaf isomorphism pulled back from the stack, not a numerical equality of degrees.

nodes.title: Generic finiteness of the extended Torelli classifying map
nodes.statement: Let k be algebraically closed, X normal integral projective over k, and C→X a stable genus-g family, g≥2, smooth over a dense open U. If U→M_g^coarse has maximal variation in the imported MC.6 sense, the composite h:X→M̄_g^coarse→A_g^min is generically finite onto its reduced integral image Z. The finite field extension K(X)/K(Z) need not be separable. No global finiteness of h or t̄ is required.
hypotheses: The classifying map is to coarse curve moduli; adding a level is not part of maximal variation.
X is integral and U is dense and nonempty; a dimension-zero X is permitted.
proofSteps: Unlevelled strong Torelli gives finite geometric fibres on the smooth locus; this follows from the same JC1 supplier used in signed-level-fibres after forgetting level.

Compose the generically quasi-finite U classifying map with this quasi-finite smooth Torelli map. The image of U is dense in h(X), so the resulting dominant map to Z has finite generic residue-field extension.
Retain the full inseparable degree. Positive-dimensional boundary fibres of t̄ do not change the generic calculation.
acceptance: An isotrivial family over a positive-dimensional X fails maximal variation; its constant h is not generically finite.
A generically finite purely inseparable base change of a maximal-variation family stays in range; no generic étaleness test is imposed.
For X a point the image dimension is0 and the finite field extension condition holds.

nodes.title: Nefness and bigness of the Hodge line under maximal variation
nodes.statement: For the family over X in maximal-variation-generic-finiteness, λ_X=det f_*ω is nef and big. Choose m,A from minimal-hodge-power, let d=dim X, Z=h(X)_red and e=[K(X):K(Z)]. Then deg_X(c₁(λ_X^⊗m)^d)=e·deg_Z(c₁(A|Z)^d)>0. Nefness follows by curve degrees; the nef-and-positive-top-intersection criterion gives bigness, and positive powers detect both properties.
hypotheses: k algebraically closed; X normal integral projective, stable genus g≥2, smooth over a dense maximal-variation open.
Big means the imported section-growth convention, and nef means nonnegative degree on every integral curve. These are generic SF.5 notions, not new definitions.
proofSteps: Use λ_X^m≅h*A. The requested generic SF.5 pullback theorem makes it nef.
Projective h is generically finite onto integral Z, so weighted cycle pushforward gives h_*[X]=e[Z]. Apply the Chern projection formula d times and the degree map, including inseparable e.

The ample restriction A|Z has positive top degree, including the degree convention in dimension0. Apply the SF.5 nef/big numerical theorem and invariance under positive power. Its transitive asymptotic-RR/Kodaira proof leaf remains visible.
acceptance: On a positive-dimensional constant family λ_X is a constant line and has zero top degree, so omitting maximal variation would fail.
On an integral projective base curve the formula is deg λ_X^m=e deg A|Z>0.
For d=0 the degree is positive and a line is big by constant section growth; no positive-dimension assumption is inserted.

nodes.title: Hodge positivity descends from a finite cover
nodes.statement: Let p:Y→X be a finite surjective morphism of normal integral projective schemes over an arbitrary field k, and C→X a stable genus-g family g≥2. Put λ_X=det f_*ω and λ_Y for its pulled-back family. Canonically λ_Y≅p*λ_X. Consequently λ_X is nef if and only if λ_Y is nef, and, when these lines are nef, λ_X is big if and only if λ_Y is big. This applies when Y is a normal stable-family cover or an already constructed finite normalization; flatness and separability of p are unnecessary.
hypotheses: Both schemes are projective over the same k; p is finite and surjective, not just dominant on an open.
The bigness equivalence here is stated for nef lines and uses top intersection, avoiding a stronger unproved general section-growth descent assertion.
proofSteps: Use arbitrary base change for the Hodge bundle and coherent determinant pullback to identify λ_Y.

For curves use a component of the finite preimage dominating each integral curve of X; degree scales by its positive field degree. This proves nef descent, and the same projection argument proves ascent.
For d=dim X use deg_Y(c₁(p*λ_X)^d)=[K(Y):K(X)]deg_X(c₁(λ_X)^d). Apply the nef/big criterion in both directions.
acceptance: For Frobenius on a smooth projective curve in characteristic p, Hodge degree scales by p; an étale-only proof fails.
For a finite nonflat cover of a singular normal projective base over k, the equality uses the full generic field degree; no flat pullback of Chow cycles is assumed.
A positive-dimensional constant family stays nonbig under any finite surjective cover; a cover cannot manufacture maximal variation.

sources.match: Finite-cover reductions in the geometric argument and the subsequent Hodge positivity argument; the general numerical transfer belongs to SF.5.

nodes.title: Hodge positivity over an arbitrary field
nodes.statement: Let k be any field, X a normal integral projective k-scheme, and f:C→X a stable genus-g family, g≥2, smooth over a dense open U. If U→M_g^coarse is generically quasi-finite onto its image, then λ_X=det f_*ω is nef and big. No perfectness or geometric-integrality assumption on k or X is imposed. The conclusion is geometric positivity of this line, not arithmetic bigness over Spec Z.
hypotheses: Normality is that of X itself; X over an algebraic closure may be nonreduced or reducible.
Use the arbitrary-field numerical/base-extension and reduced-component comparison requested from SF.5.
proofSteps: Extend to an algebraic closure k̄. For each integral component Z of (X_k̄)_red take its finite normalization Y. The Y are normal integral projective k̄-schemes; pull back the stable family and its Hodge line.

The smooth dense open and generic quasi-finiteness persist on these components. Use the permitted flat field-base-change comparison for coarse spaces, not arbitrary nonflat coarse base change. Apply hodge-nef-big-application to each Y.

Use the requested SF.5 component/reduction/normalization detection of nefness and positivity of top intersection, and flat field-extension invariance, to descend to X. Nonreduced geometric base change is treated with its generic multiplicities, not declared integral. Apply the nef/big numerical criterion on the original integral X.
acceptance: In characteristic p, X may have a finite purely inseparable field of constants over k. Its geometric base change can be nonreduced; the theorem still applies after reduction and normalization, with positive generic multiplicities.
A geometrically disconnected smooth projective X over a nonclosed k is treated componentwise after k̄, not by choosing just one component.
A constant positive-dimensional family is excluded by maximal variation even after extending k.

Precisely: for a normal integral finite-type k-scheme T and a semiabelian T-scheme G whose dense open is a principally polarized abelian scheme of dimension g and with the following polarized-trait compatibility: on every complete strictly henselian DVR mapping to T with generic point in that open, the polarized generic fibre has the positive polarized degeneration datum of C4/roadmap/polarized-degeneration-data, and its semiabelian realization agrees with the pulled-back G, give the unique extension T→A_g^min of its classifying map, the geometric abelian-part stratum formula, and a canonical identity/composition/base-change-compatible isomorphism h*A≅(det e*Ω¹_G)^m for a minimal ample A and m>0. It suffices to export this on regular atlases plus the normal overlap/base-change comparisons used here. For the stable Picard application, identify this polarized-trait datum using the semistable Jacobian degeneration interface of R11.3; this does not enter the early R11.4 semiabelian carrier prefix. Prove the contraction/independence-of-cone step: IV5.1 and5.7 do not give a toroidal lift for every normal base without a common cone. V6.7 purity is generic-characteristic-zero and cannot fill this characteristic-p gap. Preserve the C5 semiampleness/theta and Stein/base-change proof leaves. The fine-level scheme target in PEL M6 may continue to use good-prime C5; this request concerns the all-characteristic unlevelled stable Torelli target. Identify the fixed-field coarse minimal space used here and prove any required comparison with geometric fibres of the Z-model. Do not infer normality, coarse-space formation or Hodge section-ring base change just from the existence of the integral model.

Combine the existing nef-big, big-line, nef-big-numerical, weighted proper push and Chern projection interfaces into (i) pullback of an ample line along a projective generically finite morphism of integral projective k-schemes onto its reduced image is nef and big, with top degree [K(X):K(Z)]deg(A|Z)^d; (ii) nefness and, for nef lines, bigness descend and ascend under finite surjective maps of integral projective schemes. Permit inseparable field degree, nonflat finite maps and d=0. Retain the supplier’s asymptotic-RR/Kodaira proof leaf rather than treating its numerical criterion as already proof-closed. No generic positivity definitions or proofs are replanned in MC.6. Also export detection of nefness/top-intersection positivity after arbitrary field extension and passage to the reduced geometric components and their finite normalizations, retaining positive generic multiplicities for nonreduced geometric base change. This is needed to pass from algebraically closed fields to imperfect fields; no geometric-integrality shortcut is allowed.

sourceIssues.locator: Author manuscript 21 August 2024, §3.4, p.56, final Hodge-positivity paragraph; published version not collated.
sourceIssues.printed: The argument describes the restriction of compactified Torelli to the smooth moduli locus as finite.
sourceIssues.correction: Use quasi-finiteness on the smooth locus, hence generic finiteness of the maximal-variation composite. Proper finiteness to the entire Siegel target is not needed.
sourceIssues.reason: In genus2 a smooth family can specialize to a compact-type union of two elliptic curves; its Jacobian specializes to their decomposable product inside A₂. No smooth genus2 curve has that principally polarized Jacobian. Thus the smooth Torelli image is not closed in A₂ and the morphism to A₂ cannot be finite. Finite onto a locally closed image or finite-to-one wording would not have this problem.
